close_reason: Ratified review observation. The empty-state guards on metadata_changes (metadata.rs:76-80) and metadata_query_changes (metadata.rs:212-216) are intentional defence-in-depth and mirror the canonical mail-client pattern. State is a transparent newtype over String with no type-level non-emptiness enforcement; the client-side InvalidArgument is strictly more actionable than the server-side cannotCalculateChanges that would result. No code change required. Documenting the intent here serves as the defence against any future 'simplify by deleting these guards' suggestion.
description: src/methods/metadata.rs:76-80 and 212-216 reject empty-string since_state/since_query_state with InvalidArgument before the network round-trip. A future contributor might propose removing these as 'redundant with the State type', but State is a transparent newtype over String — it does not enforce non-emptiness at the type system. Without these guards the server returns 'cannotCalculateChanges' or similar, which is far less actionable than the explicit client-side error. Mirrors the canonical mail-client pattern. Defend this against simplification.
title: Defence-in-depth empty-state guards on metadata_changes and metadata_query_changes are correct
